**`boardModel.3d` is not exposed in the workout board map**

`let board = app.otherElements["boardModel.3d"]`

In the workout path the board map is `BoardMapView` (WorkoutView.swift:729), which renders `BoardModelSurface` with a non-nil `onContactTap`. In `BoardModelSurface.body` (BoardModelView.swift:79-87) the `boardModel.3d` identifier is only attached when `onContactTap == nil`; with a tap handler the identifier is deliberately omitted so the per-contact identifiers stay visible. Use the workout map's own identifier (`boardMap.presentationSelector` is already used at line 257, or the `boardDetail.map`/`boardMap` element) instead of `boardModel.3d`.

⚠️ **Potential issue** · Important

**New *.xcresult.zip LFS rule never applies to the retained bundles**

`*.xcresult.zip filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text`

The retained result bundles this rule is meant to cover live under `docs/source-audits/.../validation/*.xcresult.zip` (e.g. `docs/source-audits/2026-09-29-remaining-cad/additional-placid-badger-final-validation-2026-10-03/validation/plateau-layout-red.xcresult.zip`), and `docs/source-audits/` is already excluded by `.gitignore` (the audit READMEs and `artifact-inventory.json` are force-added). Git attributes are only consulted for paths that are actually added, so for these files the rule is inert: they are either never committed, or committed via `git add -f` and stored as full binary blobs in the pack instead of LFS pointers. The PR description claims "Retained exact Xcode result bundles" are LFS-tracked, so the intent is not achieved. Either un-ignore the specific retained bundle paths (or add a negation such as `!docs/source-audits/**/*.xcresult.zip`) so the attribute applies, or drop the rule and document that these archives are intentionally not LFS-managed.

⚠️ **Potential issue** · Important

**`edge-reverse-06mm-flat` camera looks at the back of the selected face**

`"viewDirection": [0, 0, 1]`
This pose's rotation is `[1, 0, 0, 0]` (180° about X), so the board's front face is turned away from the viewer, yet the camera direction is the same `[0, 0, 1]` used by the upright `edge-front-*` poses. The sibling `edge-reverse-10mm-*` poses in this same file correctly use `[0, 0, 1]` with rotation `[1, 0, 0, 0]`… but note `edge-reverse-10mm-incut`/`-flat` are the ones with `[1,0,0,0]` and `[0,1,0,0]` respectively — here `edge-reverse-06mm-flat` has rotation `[1,0,0,0]` while `edge-reverse-06mm-incut` has `[0,1,0,0]`, i.e. the two 6 mm reverse poses have their rotations swapped relative to the 10 mm pair. With the rotation applied to the camera (`SuspendedBoardPresentation.makeCameraFraming`), the viewer ends up behind the newly presented face — exactly the failure family `Tools/HangboardPackages/tests/test_pose_camera_facing.py` was written to catch (it lists `nature-stone-hanger` in its docstring but only parametrizes `frictitious-nug`/`port-a-board`/`yy-*`, so this pose is not covered). Swap the two rotations (or the two view directions) so the reverse poses face their selected contacts.

⚠️ **Potential issue** · Important

**Pose/base composition order differs from the renderer**

`let world = transform * SIMD4<Float>(...)`

`transform` here is `SuspendedBoardPresentation.boardTransform(for: pose)` (the pose matrix), and the point fed in is the base-transformed bounds center. The renderer composes the other way: `SuspendedBoardPresentation.solve(pose:suspension:BoardModelCADRoutedCord...)` builds `boardTransform(pose) * modelTransform` (per the PR briefing), i.e. base first, then pose. So this helper computes `pose * base * center` while the rendered instance is at `pose * base` applied to the model — the two disagree whenever the pose rotation is not identity.

Effect: `placed` is sorted by the resulting `world.x` and then mapped `[.left: placed[0], .right: placed[1]]`, so a wrong x ordering silently assigns the left hand to the physically right unit (and vice versa) for the two-instance `cadRoutedCord` boards. The `first.side == nil || first.side?.rawValue == firstSide.rawValue` guard only catches this when the contacts carry an authored `side`; for the reusable units (which are exactly the ones with `equipmentObjectID`-based identity and no authored side) it passes and the swap goes unnoticed. Please confirm the intended order against `SuspendedBoardPresentation.solve` and make this helper use the same composition.

⚠️ **Potential issue** · Important

**Stale selectedPositionID sizes the map for the wrong pose**

`aspectRatio: content.presentation.aspectRatio(for: selectedPositionID)`

`selectedPositionID` is an externally-owned `@Binding` that this view only writes in `updateSelectedPosition()` (onAppear / hold change / board change / rotation-selector set). It is never re-derived when the *presentation* changes through the picker: `selectPresentation(_:)` calls `presentationSelection.selectPresentation(id:on:)` and then `updateSelectedPosition()`, but `updateSelectedPosition()` reads `presentationSelection.presentationID` — the `@State` that was just mutated — so the binding is not updated in that same pass. The body re-evaluates immediately with the new `content.presentation` but the old `selectedPositionID`, so `aspectRatio(for:)` takes the `cadRoutedCord` branch with a position ID that does not belong to the new presentation (`suspension.canonicalPoses[positionID]` misses) and falls through to the generic `media.orientation` framing. For a board whose presentations have different cord framings the map is then sized with the wrong aspect ratio until the next hold/rotation change. Deriving the position locally in `mapContent` (as `BoardDetailMapView` already does) and passing that value to `aspectRatio(for:)` avoids the one-pass lag.
